summary: Lorna Dewaraja worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Ceylon (~1949–1952) and the University of London (~1966–1969). Her career included posts at the University of Ceylon, University of Colombo (~1969–1989), and St Anne's College.

Sinologist and art historian Lothar Ledderose studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Princeton, Harvard, Tokyo, and Cologne. His main appointments included positions at Princeton, Harvard, the National Palace Museum, and a long tenure as professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2010).

Lothar von Falkenhausen specializes in sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Bonn, Peking University, Kyoto, and Harvard. In 1993, he became a full professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, later serving as associate director (2004–2011).

Louis Dumont worked in indology and religious studies, studying at EPHE, the Institut d'ethnologie, and under Marcel Mauss, Walther Schubring, and Alain Froment. He held posts at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires, Oxford (1951–1955), and EHESS (1955).

Louis Finot worked in indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École des chartes and under Sylvain Lévi. He was director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1898) and held posts at the EPHE and Collège de France.
Louis Gabaude is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 1978 to 2007.

Louis Gernet worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1902–1905) and held positions at the University of Algiers (~1917–1948) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1948–1962).

Louis H. Gray was a scholar in linguistics, indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Princeton (~1892–1896) and Columbia (~1896–1900), and held posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (1921).

Louis Havet was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1872) under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. He served as professor and Latin philology chair at the Collège de France (1885–1925).

Louis Renou was an indologist and linguist. He studied at the Sorbonne, ENLOV, and EPHE under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch. He held professorships and directorships at the University of Lyon, the University of Paris/Sorbonne, and EPHE.

Louis de La Vallée Poussin worked in Buddhist studies and indology. He studied at Liège, KU Leuven, the Sorbonne, and Leiden under Lévi, Kern, Harlez, Colinet, and Henry. He served as professor at Ghent University (1893–1929).

Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and sinology. He studied at the Collège de France under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He was director and Persian chair at INALCO and chief keeper at the Bibliothèque nationale.

Louise Allison Cort is a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College (~1967–1969) and served as a ceramics curator at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries (~1981–2020).

Louise Child works in religious studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Leeds, where she completed her PhD under Linda Hogan and also studied under Ringu Tulku; she subsequently held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University (attested 1999) under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma, having also studied under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Lourens P. van den Bosch worked in indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Groningen (1965–1971) and Utrecht University (~1970–1978) under Jan Gonda and other teachers, and held an assistant post at Groningen (1968–1971).
Lozang Samten studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Luboš Bělka specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from ~1977 to 1982 and held a post there beginning around 1993.
Luca Brigada Villa specializes in linguistics, indology, and computational linguistics. He has held academic posts at the University of Bergamo and the University of Pavia.
